item.title: SoftBank’s $40 Billion Loan for OpenAI Stake Gets 21 New Lenders
item.description: SoftBank Group Corp.’s $40 billion bridge loan for its investment in US tech giant OpenAI has attracted a new group of 21 lenders in a broader syndication phase, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: CXMT Can Rally More Than 1,200% on Market Share Win, Nomura Says
item.description: China’s memory-chip bellwether CXMT Corp. can extend its blockbuster stock market debut to rally 1,239% from its initial public offering price as it wins market share over time, according to Nomura Holdings Inc.

item.title: Indonesia’s Acting Central Bank Chief Damayanti Seen as Reassuring for Investors
item.description: Destry Damayanti, announced as acting chief of Bank Indonesia Monday, is a trained economist whose monetary policy experience may comfort investors rattled by the sudden resignation of Governor Perry Warjiyo.

item.title: Warjiyo’s Departure Raises Scrutiny on BI Policy, Analysts Say
item.description: Bank Indonesia Governor Perry Warjiyo’s resignation is expected to heighten uncertainty and volatility across the nation’s financial markets, with analysts citing concerns over policy direction and central bank independence.

item.title: CATL Surges After Share Buyback Plan, Strong First-Half Profit
item.description: Contemporary Amperex Technology Co. Ltd. shares jumped in China after the world’s biggest electric-vehicle battery manufacturer unveiled a buyback plan following strong earnings for the first half.

item.title: Trip.com Shares Jump in Hong Kong as Regulatory Overhang Clears
item.description: Trip.com Group Ltd. posted its biggest gain in nearly a year after the outcome of its antitrust investigation largely matched expectations, lifting a key overhang on the stock even as the company was hit with a hefty fine.

item.title: India Retail Investors Cash Out as Foreign Buying of Stocks Resumes
item.description: Selling by retail investors could limit potential upside in the Nifty benchmark.

item.title: Instagram, Facebook Ran AI ‘Nudify’ Ads from China, Report Says
item.description: Meta Platforms Inc.’s Facebook and Instagram have served thousands of ads for AI “nudify” apps in breach of the company’s policies, delivered by one of its few advertising partners in China, according to the nonprofit Tech Transparency Project.

item.title: China Chipmakers See 2,580% Profit Jump as Economic Split Widens
item.description: China’s industry saw profit gains slow for a second month even as sectors benefiting from the tech boom enjoy a windfall, adding to evidence of an uneven recovery for companies across parts of the world’s second-biggest economy.

item.title: SK Hynix Listing Emboldens Korea’s Drive to Repatriate Dollars
item.description: A strong rebound in the won driven in part by SK Hynix Inc.’s record US listing has given South Korean authorities fresh impetus to prod exporters to repatriate their overseas dollars.

item.title: China’s Moonshot to Release Breakthrough AI Model for Download
item.description: Moonshot AI is poised to make its Kimi K3 model available for public download, expanding its reach and influence in the global open software community at a time of growing US concern about Chinese encroachment into the top echelons of AI development.

item.title: Indonesia Central Bank Chief Warjiyo Unexpectedly Resigns
item.description: Bank Indonesia Governor Perry Warjiyo suddenly resigned for unspecified “personal reasons,” unnerving investors who had viewed the central banker as a stabilizing force in an economy whipsawed by the policies of President Prabowo Subianto.

item.title: Major Brands Sell China Tomatoes as Aussie-Grown, ABC Says
item.description: Several major food brands in Australia are selling tomato products grown in China as domestically produced, with forensic testing showing some are sourced from the Xinjiang region, according to an investigation by the Australian Broadcasting Corp.

item.title: Blackstone Unit to Buy HSBC’s Australian Loan Book, AFR Says
item.description: Blackstone Inc.’s private credit division is set to buy HSBC Holdings Plc’s A$30 billion-plus ($21 billion) Australian loan book, the Australian Financial Review reports.

item.title: Woodside’s $34 Billion Browse Named State Significant Project
item.description: Woodside Energy Group Ltd.’s A$48.7 billion ($34 billion) Browse gas field development has been declared a State Significant Project, allowing for expedited approvals from the Western Australia government.

item.title: Singapore Delivers Back-to-Back Tightening to Tame Price Risks
item.description: Singapore’s central bank tightened policy further on Monday, bracing for expected inflationary pressures as renewed tensions in the Middle East threaten to keep energy prices elevated.

item.title: China’s Pork Market Recovery Struggles to Overcome Tepid Demand
item.description: The Chinese government’s campaign to lift pork prices is finally gaining traction. But the rally is running into a familiar obstacle: consumers still aren’t buying enough.

item.title: Chinese Biotech Overtakes AI as Emerging-Market Growth Trade
item.description: As the artificial-intelligence rally sputters in emerging markets, investors searching for high-growth alternatives are turning to Chinese biotech.

item.title: Nvidia in Talks on $250 Billion Backing for OpenAI Hub, WSJ Says
item.description: Nvidia Corp.’s in discussions to provide a guarantee of about $250 billion to help OpenAI lease computing from a giant data center project, the Wall Street Journal reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

item.title: EQT Lifts Takeover Offer for Perpetual to $1.8 Billion
item.description: EQT AB sweetened its takeover bid for Australian investment management firm Perpetual Ltd. to around A$2.6 billion ($1.8 billion).

item.title: Marcos Needs State of the Nation to Revive Philippine Economy, Presidency
item.description: A year ago, Philippines President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.’s annual address to Congress shocked the nation with revelations of billions of dollars of graft involving flood-control schemes. The disclosure triggered an economic slump as projects slowed and consumers and businesses cut spending.

item.title: China Memory Champion CXMT Set to Debut After $9.8 Billion IPO
item.description: CXMT Corp. is set to begin trading in Shanghai on Monday after raising 66.6 billion yuan ($9.8 billion) in the second-largest initial public offering in China’s history, with potential for a first-day gain that would make it the largest company in the country.

item.title: Gold Climbs as Pause in Mideast Fighting Curbs Inflation Risk
item.description: Gold rose, after a pause in fighting between the US and Iran over the weekend eased oil supply risks and inflationary concerns.

item.title: Inside The Six-Year Fight to Reopen a Hollywood Movie Palace
item.description: A 26-year-old actor rallied, protested and eventually cajoled a secretive family into a deal

item.title: Oil Dips, Stock Futures Rise as Iran Tensions Ease: Markets Wrap
item.description: Oil dropped and US equity-index futures rallied as the US and Iran refrained from retaliatory strikes, easing concerns over potential disruptions to Middle East energy supplies after a recent escalation in the conflict.

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for July 27
item.description: ⁠⁠Oil sank after the US paused strikes against Iran, easing Middle East tensions even as the Houthis claimed attacks against Saudi targets.

item.title: Kiwi Will Outpace Euro on Widening Rate Gap, Strategists Say
item.description: New Zealand’s dollar is set to rise to the strongest in more than a year against the euro due to expectations the local central bank will outpace its European peer in raising interest rates, according to strategists.

item.title: Kioxia Faces More Volatility as Leveraged ETFs Hit Japan Stocks
item.description: Kioxia Holdings Corp. faces more wild price swings with leveraged exchange-traded funds tracking the Japanese memory chipmaker’s shares set to be listed in the US.

item.title: Bond Traders on Edge as Risks of Fed Rate Hike This Week Mount
item.description: Bond traders enter the week seeing a better than one-in-three chance that the Federal Reserve hikes interest rates on Wednesday after flaring Middle East tensions lifted oil prices, boosting inflation worries and yields.

item.title: Fed Faces Growing Pressure to Hike Rates as Price Risks Rebound
item.description: Federal Reserve officials will head into their policy meeting this week confronting a resurgence in price pressures that could make their decision on whether to hold or hike interest rates a close call — and a contentious one.
